title: Choose the visual world for viruchith.com
question: The roll assigned The Manual Page. Keep it, take the pick, take the category standard, or re-roll. Every card already honours your brief: neutral light and dark themes, typography-led, rigorous grid, hairline structure, sparing accent, no gradients, glows, or shadows.

options.label: The Manual Page
options.thesis: The whole site reads as viruchith(1): a precisely typeset manual for one engineer, every claim cross-referenced to its evidence.
options.viewport: A running header (VIRUCHITH(1), Backend Engineering, Bengaluru) over NAME, which sets name and role as the display line; SYNOPSIS carries the working Email and Resume actions as real buttons; DESCRIPTION opens the proof with 100,000+ requests/day linked to its write-up.
options.risk: A manual can read as an inside joke to recruiters; plain-English section labels must lead, with the man-page ritual as structure rather than costume.

raised.raise: One shared unit: every rule, baseline, and gap snaps to a single 4px unit, images included.
Density courage: articles and projects run as dense ruled lists, two columns at wide widths, never airy card grids.
Figures pinned to claims: every metric is set in tabular digits beside the claim it measures and links to its evidence.
Inversion as state: hover, selected, and pressed states invert ink and paper instead of glowing or tinting.
Addressable everything: each section and entry carries a stable visible anchor id for deep links.
Depth by overlap only: a surface over a hairline is the only elevation; no shadows in either theme.

options.label: Swiss Grid Systems
options.lineage: International Typographic Style, Müller-Brockmann grid systems
options.thesis: A strict modular grid where size, weight, and position carry all hierarchy, and nothing else is allowed to.
options.viewport: An asymmetric grid: name and role set large across seven columns, a narrow column of facts (location, availability, certification) at right, Email and Resume aligned to the same baseline as the first fact.
options.risk: This is where most runs land for a Vercel-inspired brief; it sits closest to the reference and turns generic quickly if the grid is not exact.

options.label: Pixorama Metropolis
options.thesis: Your systems as a zoomable pixel city of services and queues.
options.viewport: A pixel city of microservices with hover labels.
options.case: Fuses poorly: full-saturation colour and illustration break the neutral brief, and recruiters do not read a city as a CV.
options.kept: One shared unit that every element snaps to.

options.label: Penny-Press Broadside
options.thesis: Each article as the day's broadside, rammed into two columns.
options.viewport: A shouting headline over an engraving band and dense verse.
options.case: Fuses poorly: relief illustration and alarm colour contradict the minimal brief; tone misreads for a hiring page.
options.risk: Theatrical where the brief asks for precision.

options.label: Collider Event Display
options.thesis: One request traced through the system like a collision event.
options.viewport: A frozen request event with tracks through service layers.
options.case: Fuses unevenly: strong for engineers, but signal colours, glow, and WebGL motion break the brief, and recruiters lose the thread.
options.risk: Spectacle that hides the hiring action.
options.kept: Figures pinned to the claims they measure.

options.label: HyperCard Stack
options.thesis: The portfolio as a stack of linked one-bit cards.
options.viewport: A home card with painted buttons to each stack.
options.case: Fuses partly: neutral enough, but card-by-card navigation hides the page's proof and contradicts the brief's no-cards rule.

options.label: Miura-Fold Sheet
options.thesis: A compact packet that unfolds into the full engineering record.
options.viewport: A folded packet that deploys on pull.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the unfolding ritual delays the hiring action and needs motion the brief rules out.
options.kept: Stable visible ids on every block.

options.label: Łowicz Papercut
options.thesis: Sections built up as pasted colour layers.
options.viewport: A symmetrical roundel as the hero.
options.case: Fuses poorly: saturated folk colour and ornament contradict the neutral, engineered brief.
options.kept: Depth by overlap, never by shadow.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The Vercel-school developer portfolio, played straight at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: A centred grotesk headline over a black Email button, then a hairline grid of featured projects.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from many developer portfolios by design, and the closest to cloning the reference.
